liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Called tasty, followed by a smooth transition into Dancin'; Played in a very peppy fashion [15][17]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Reviewer says this is the earliest show they found with Dire Wolf played at a faster tempo [14]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer finds the drum segment fantastic [16]
- Reviewer finds this version a total surprise, following the silky transition from Eyes [15]
- Particularly strong version, though shorter than most others [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Black Peter**: back after 115 archived shows (1078 days) [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-01.123211.sbd.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 163 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.gmb.86234.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [3]
- **gd77-10-01.sbd.unknown.277.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: A pop in the recording turns up around 1:33 into this song; Opener suffers sound problems and a big tape cut, then jumps straight into the next song; A second large cut falls in this song, right after the opener's cut [9][11][13]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.ashley-bertha.10689.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: Bass is so heavy and prominent that most home systems struggle; reviewer suggests flattening the bass EQ; Scratchy distortion appears here, which reviewer guesses comes from Jerry's newly refurbished guitar; The bass-heavy sound overwhelmed a small 30-watt Sony shelf system [18][19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls it essential listening alongside the next night's show on 10-2-77 [8]
- Overshadowed by 10/2, which has better song sets and longer jams like Wheel into Truckin into Other One [13]
- Suggests momentum toward the 10/29/77 peak began here, with the band stretching out beyond spring's more formal style [15]
- Reviewer rates it as good as any 1977 show heard, including the Barton Hall show [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-01.123211.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat [1]. Also: Most of the static in this song was cleaned up in this version [1]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.gmb.86234.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer..Transferred and mastered by ChrisL.; source: Betty Board (see comments) [3]. Also: Chain runs from a 7-inch two-track reel with DBX-1 at 7.5 ips through PCM501ES to a Fostex D5 master DAT [3]
- **gd77-10-01.sbd.unknown.277.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.ashley-bertha.10689.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bertha Remaster of the Betty Board source; source: SBD>>MR>>PCM>>DAT>>CDA>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA [5]. Also: Digitally remastered April 16, 2002 by an archive.org user on a custom dual-DAW nicknamed Bertha [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by George Alper Grateful Dead: [1977-10-01 Paramount Theater, Portland, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1977-10-01-paramount-theater-portland-or-usa/) [21]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1977-10-01 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1977-10-01-backstage-pass/) [22]
